subject: science
topic: Most of the ocean floor has never been seen
angle: Humanity has visually observed a minuscule and geographically biased fraction of the deep seafloor, with the vast majority of mapping efforts concentrated near only five countries.
title: The Unseen Ocean Floor

hooks.text: How much of the ocean floor have you actually seen?
You think the ocean is mapped. It is not.
You accept a world view shaped by only five nations.
A small light moves through cold, dark water.
0.001% of the deep seafloor is seen.

reveal.headline: You have seen less than 0.001% of the deep seafloor.
reveal.body: The area we have visually observed is approximately a tenth of the size of Belgium. Most of the rest remains unseen.

explain.headline: Observation is concentrated in five countries.
explain.body: Ninety-seven percent of all deep-sea dives are conducted by the United States, Japan, New Zealand, France, and Germany. This creates a heavy geographical bias in what we know.

matters.headline: Our map of the world is incomplete.
matters.body: That may be why our understanding of the planet is shaped by a few specific nations. We are looking at a tiny window of the total ocean.

example.headline: You look at a map on a screen.
example.body: You see a blue expanse and assume the world is charted. You do not see the parts that remain blank and unvisited.

question.headline: What exists in the parts we refuse to look at?

stat.label: of the deep seafloor visually observed by humanity

claims.text: We have visually observed less than 0.001% of the deep seafloor, which is an area approximately a tenth of the size of Belgium.
claims.quote: we have visually observed less than 0.001%, a total area approximately a tenth of the size of Belgium.

claims.text: Sixty-five percent of all in situ visual seafloor observations in the dataset were within 200 nm of only three countries: the United States, Japan, and New Zealand.
claims.quote: Sixty-five percent of all in situ visual seafloor observations in our dataset were within 200 nm of only three countries: the United States, Japan, and New Zealand.

claims.text: Ninety-seven percent of all dives compiled have been conducted by just five countries: the United States, Japan, New Zealand, France, and Germany.
claims.quote: Ninety-seven percent of all dives we compiled have been conducted by just five countries: the United States, Japan, New Zealand, France, and Germany.

claims.text: With the current average rate of new map generation of ∼3.2% of total seafloor area annually, the global seafloor could be mapped in approximately 20 years.
claims.quote: With the current average rate of new map generation of ∼3.2% of total seafloor area annually, we predict that the global seafloor could be mapped in approximately 20 years.

claims.text: Over 14% of the ocean fell under the category of globally important marine areas and most of this area (88%) is not yet protected.

verdict: The evidence confirms that direct visual observation of the deep seafloor is extremely limited and heavily skewed toward specific nations.
caveat: The data highlights a significant geographical bias in observation rather than a total lack of mapping effort in all regions.
caption:
The vast majority of the deep seafloor remains hidden from human eyes.

Research shows we have visually observed less than 0.001% of the deep seafloor, with observations heavily skewed toward five specific countries. The data highlights a geographical bias in observation rather than a total lack of mapping effort.

What part of the world do you think remains a mystery?
